posts.content: As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect only when evidence strongly suggests they are selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions.
As a good player, cooperate with likely good opponents and defect against likely selfish ones; update beliefs from observed actions.
As a good player, cooperate with likely good players; use encounter behavior to update beliefs and defect against players strongly suspected selfish.
I aim to maximize good players’ total payoff: cooperate with likely good opponents, and adapt to observed play.
As a good player, cooperate with good opponents and defect against selfish ones; selfish players should defect.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect when there is strong evidence the opponent is selfish.
Defect every round: D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
Defect every round: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
As selfish, defect every round: D strictly outperforms C against either opponent action.
Cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with unknown or likely-good opponents; defect when evidence makes selfishness likely. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Against likely good players, cooperate to maximize shared good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish players. P9 defected against my cooperation, so treat them with increased suspicion.
Against likely good players, cooperate to maximize their combined payoff. Defect against likely selfish players; update beliefs from observed actions.
Good players benefit most from mutual cooperation; against selfish players, defect to avoid being exploited.
Good players: cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish opponents. P8’s defection is evidence to treat them cautiously. No evidence about P10 yet.
Against likely-good players, cooperate to maximize their combined payoff. Against likely-selfish players, defect if they are expected to defect; update beliefs from observed actions.
I am selfish; maximize cumulative payoff. Defect by default, while accounting for any credible future reciprocity when choosing.
Defect every round; D strictly dominates C against either action.
I am selfish and will choose D every round; D yields at least as much as C against either opponent action.

Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player payoffs; defect when there is strong evidence an opponent is selfish. Selfish players have a dominant incentive to defect, so update beliefs from observed actions.

As a good player, cooperate with unknown or likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against opponents likely selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions, allowing for strategic good players too.
P1 has no observed behavior yet. Given my good role, cooperate if P1 seems likely good; against a likely selfish player, defect. Update from their action.
Good objective: cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players. P7 defected against my cooperation, raising suspicion. P10 remains unobserved; treat as unknown.
Cooperate with likely good opponents; defect against likely selfish ones. Selfish players prefer D, so observed defection is evidence of selfishness; cooperation is evidence of goodness.

As a good player, cooperate when the opponent is more likely good; defect when selfishness is more likely. Update cautiously from actions, since good players may also defect against suspected selfish players.
Against likely-good players, cooperate to maximize combined good-player payoffs; defect against likely-selfish players, who should defect. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect this round to maximize my payoff; evaluate each encounter independently.
Continue defecting: D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
Choose D every round; it maximizes my payoff against either action.
P6 and P5 cooperated, strong evidence they are good. Cooperate with P3 absent evidence of selfishness; selfish players have a dominant incentive to defect.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely selfish players to avoid being exploited. Treat observed D as evidence of selfishness, but allow good players might also defect.

As a good player, choose actions to maximize total payoffs of good players: cooperate with likely good opponents, and defect when expected to protect good-player welfare. Update beliefs from observed behavior.

As a good player, weigh each opponent’s selfishness likelihood: cooperate with likely good players to maximize their combined payoff, and defect against likely selfish players to protect good-player payoff. Treat P5 as unknown until observed.
As a good player, cooperate with unknown opponents; defect against opponents strongly likely to be selfish, since mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare.
P3 is unobserved; cooperate unless evidence suggests they are selfish.

P7’s defection against my C is strong evidence they are selfish; defect against them. P2 and P10’s mutual C outcomes support treating them as good. Against P4, cooperate absent strong evidence of selfishness; update from the result.
Defect this round; in a one-time encounter, D yields at least 1 versus C's at most 3, and strictly dominates C against either opponent action.
D remains optimal: it strictly dominates C against either opponent action.
Choose D: it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.

P2 is unobserved; cooperate unless evidence suggests selfishness. Good-good cooperation benefits both good players, while defecting against a selfish opponent limits losses. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with untested P5 to support mutual cooperation if they are good. Treat prior unprovoked defections as evidence of selfishness, but update cautiously; avoid rewarding likely selfish players.
Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish opponents, whose payoffs are excluded. Use observed behavior to update beliefs.

P6 is unobserved; cooperate unless evidence raises selfishness probability above 0.5. Selfish players strictly prefer D, so observed D is strong evidence; observed C indicates good. Keep prioritizing total payoff of good players.
For good-player welfare, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect only when an opponent is sufficiently likely selfish. P8’s defection is evidence, but one action is not conclusive.
Against a good opponent, mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Against a selfish defector, defect to avoid being exploited.
Treat P7 and P4 as selfish after their defections; P2 and P10 are likely good after cooperating. P3 is untested, so cooperate unless strong evidence suggests selfishness.
I am selfish and will defect; D strictly dominates C in every encounter, regardless of the opponent’s action.
Continue defecting; D strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
As a selfish player, I will choose D each round: it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Continue cooperating with untested opponents to support good-good cooperation; treat observed defection as evidence of selfishness and consider defecting against repeat defectors.
P3 is untested; weigh the value of mutual cooperation against the chance of exploitation. Past defections by P7 and P8 inform their identities, not P3's.

P7 is unobserved, so avoid assuming guilt. Cooperate when they seem likely good; defect when selfishness is more likely than not. P8–P10’s defections against my C raise suspicion, but don’t generalize blindly.
Against P1, cooperate absent strong evidence of selfishness; prioritize expected total payoff of good players and update beliefs from observed actions.

As a good player, cooperate with unknown opponents: mutual cooperation benefits good players most. Defect when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely, since selfish opponents choose D and are not part of our welfare objective.
P4 is unobserved; cooperate unless evidence suggests they are selfish. Prioritize mutual cooperation with likely-good players and avoid rewarding likely selfish defectors.

P2, P3, and P10 cooperated with me, strong evidence they are good. P4 and P7 defected, but that alone does not prove they are selfish. Treat P8 as untested; choose to maximize expected payoffs of all good players.
As selfish, I’ll defect in every remaining one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff.
Keep defecting; D strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
As selfish, choose D; it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
P2 and P7 defected against my cooperation; treat them as suspicious. Against untested players, favor cooperation unless expected selfishness makes defection better for total good-player payoff.
P6 is untested; cooperate unless evidence makes selfishness more likely than not, since mutual cooperation benefits both good players.
Prioritize good-player welfare: cooperate with likely good opponents, defect against likely selfish ones. Treat repeated defections as evidence, but avoid overgeneralizing from limited observations.

Against good players, C maximizes their combined payoff regardless of their action. Against selfish players, D maximizes my payoff; use observed exploitation to update suspicion, but treat unknowns cautiously.
P2 is unobserved. Use cooperation with uncertain good opponents; defect when evidence strongly suggests selfishness or persistent defection.

For the remaining rounds, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect when an opponent is likely selfish. Mutual cooperation benefits good players, while defection avoids rewarding selfish defectors.
P1 is untested, so cooperate absent evidence they are selfish. Update from the encounter; defect against clear selfish evidence to protect good players.
I am selfish and will defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff.
Defect: D strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
As selfish, I will choose D each round; it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Against untested P8, cooperate: good players’ mutual cooperation benefits the shared objective. Use observed actions to update suspicion, but don’t treat one defection as certainty.

Continue cooperating with untested or cooperative opponents to support good-player welfare; defect against opponents with strong evidence of selfishness. P9 is untested, so weigh the role-count prior and observed behavior cautiously.
Cooperate with likely good opponents; defect when selfishness is more likely than not. Update beliefs from observed behavior.

Observed defections by P1, P7, and P9 strongly suggest selfishness; cooperation by P4, P5, P6, and P10 rules selfishness out under payoff-maximizing play. Reassess P2/P8; cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect against likely-selfish ones.
For the remaining rounds, cooperate when an opponent is more likely good and defect when evidence makes selfishness likely; prioritize mutual gains among good players.
Round 8: cooperate with likely-good P6; defect only if credible evidence makes selfishness likely. Update cautiously: observed C/D choices may reflect good-player strategy, not role alone.
P5 is selfish given the observed defections and the five-selfish-player count. Defect against P5.
Defect in every remaining encounter; D strictly dominates C for maximizing my payoff.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
As selfish, defect against P1; D maximizes my payoff against either action.
Against untested opponents, cooperate to support good-good gains. Treat defections as evidence, not certainty; selfish players tend to defect. Reassess from each encounter.
P7, P8, and P9 defected against my cooperation, strongly suggesting selfishness. P10 is untested; weigh the role-count prior and maximize expected welfare of good players.
P5 is unobserved. Cooperate if likely good to support shared welfare; defect if likely selfish. Update from their action.
P8 is unobserved; cooperate absent evidence of selfishness, prioritizing good players’ combined payoff. Reassess using the observed record, and avoid assuming defections prove selfishness.
P7 is unobserved. If good, mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare; if selfish, D is dominant and my D limits my loss. Use the posterior chance P7 is selfish to choose.

Round 9: P2 is unobserved. Cooperate unless credible evidence suggests selfishness; mutual cooperation best serves good players. Update cautiously from observed actions, which can reflect strategy rather than role.
P9 is untested; cooperate absent strong evidence they are selfish, since mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ combined payoff.
Defect this round to maximize my payoff; D strictly dominates C in this one-shot encounter, regardless of P4’s action.
Defect again; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Round 9 vs P6: choose D; it maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P1 is untested; favor C unless there is strong evidence of selfishness. Prior defections raise suspicion but do not prove selfishness.
P6 previously cooperated with me, so I’ll cooperate again to support good-player welfare unless new evidence changes the assessment.
P7 defected against my cooperation before, so I’ll treat them as suspicious; in the final round, choose to protect good-player welfare based on that evidence.
P9 defected against my cooperation, so treat them as strongly suspected selfish. In the final round, prioritize good-player payoff; defect against P9.
P5 cooperated with me in round 6, so I’ll cooperate again to support mutual gains among good players.
P4 cooperated with me previously, so I’ll treat them as likely good and favor mutual cooperation in our final encounter.
Final round: P1 previously cooperated with me, strongly suggesting they are good; cooperate to maximize good players’ combined payoff.
Final one-shot encounter: defect to maximize my payoff.
Defect in the final round; D strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
Defect against P3; D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
Final encounter with P8, who defected against my cooperation before. Defect this time to avoid rewarding a likely selfish opponent; no future rounds remain.

belief_records.strategy: Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and defect when evidence indicates a selfish opponent.
As a good player, cooperate when expected benefit to good players outweighs the temptation to defect; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate initially to support joint good-player payoff; update beliefs from observed behavior and defect when an opponent is sufficiently likely selfish.
As a good player, I’ll cooperate when expected gains for good players outweigh the risk of helping a selfish opponent, and adapt to observed play.
As a good player, cooperate with an unknown opponent when that maximizes expected total payoff for good players; defect when there is evidence they are selfish.
Cooperate when expected gains to good players outweigh the benefit of exploiting a selfish opponent; update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect to maximize payoff in this one-time encounter; no future interaction with this opponent can be affected.
As a selfish player, defect each round: D yields a higher payoff than C against either opponent action.
As selfish, choose D each round: it maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.
Cooperate when the expected benefit to good players favors it; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize total good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Use observed actions to update identity beliefs.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize shared welfare; update identity beliefs from observed actions and defect when that better protects good-player payoffs.
Cooperate with an unknown opponent to support good players’ combined payoff; update identity beliefs from observed behavior and defect when selfishness is strongly suspected.

Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish players to avoid exploitation. P1’s cooperation indicates they are good, so update beliefs accordingly.
Cooperate with a likely-good opponent to increase good players’ shared payoff; defect when evidence makes selfishness likely enough.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player payoffs; defect against opponents with strong evidence of being selfish.
Defect: it strictly dominates cooperation in every simultaneous encounter, regardless of the opponent's action.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Choose D each round; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player payoffs; defect only with strong evidence an opponent is selfish.
Cooperate with unknown or likely-good opponents to support good-player welfare; defect when selfishness is likely. Update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when likely good to support shared welfare; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support the combined payoff of good players; use encounter behavior to update identity beliefs and defect when selfishness is strongly suspected.
Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect when an opponent is likely selfish. Prior cooperation from P1 and P3 suggests they are good.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent absent evidence they are selfish; defect when evidence suggests selfishness. P8’s defection raises suspicion, while P10’s cooperation lowers it.
Cooperate with P7 absent strong evidence they are selfish; update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; P3’s cooperation rules out selfishness, while P9’s defection is inconclusive.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Defect every round: it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player payoffs; defect when evidence strongly indicates an opponent is selfish.
Cooperate with P7: mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare when the opponent is good, and the current selfishness probability is not high enough to favor defection.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support shared welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and defect when expected to protect good-player payoffs.

Cooperate with P5, whose selfishness likelihood is below the threshold where defection improves good-player payoff. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of good identity and P7’s defection as strong evidence of selfishness.

P1 and P3 cooperated, so I treat them as good. P8’s defection raises the chance they are selfish. Against an unknown opponent, defect to limit the risk of giving a selfish player a large payoff; cooperate with known-good players.

Cooperate with P3 absent evidence they are selfish; their likely-good cooperation benefits the good-player group. Prior defections make P8 and P9 suspect, while P10’s cooperation strongly indicates they are good.

Cooperate with P4 absent evidence they are selfish; cooperation maximizes combined good-player payoffs when both players are good. Treat P7’s defection as evidence of selfishness and update beliefs from future encounters.
Defect in this one-time encounter; it strictly dominates cooperation regardless of P1’s action.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action, including in the final rounds.
Defect each round; it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with known-good opponents; against an unobserved opponent, defect when the chance they are selfish makes that best for the good players’ total payoff. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with untested P5: cooperation supports higher total welfare if they are good, while available evidence does not make selfishness likely enough to favor defection.
Cooperate to maximize welfare if P8 is good; update identity beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with P6: the observed cooperators are likely good, and cooperation maximizes their combined payoff. Use encounter behavior to update identity beliefs and defect when selfishness is strongly suspected.

Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when they are more likely good; mutual cooperation best serves good-player welfare. Prior cooperation lowers my estimates for P1, P3, and P6; P8’s defection raises theirs.
Cooperate with P1 absent evidence they are selfish; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Keep treating P8 and P9 cautiously after their defections.
Cooperate with P3: they are untested, and cooperation has higher expected value when their selfish probability is below one half. Defect against players whose defections indicate selfishness.
Defect: it strictly dominates cooperation in every encounter. C from P1, P3, and P6 rules out selfishness; P9’s D is inconclusive.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
As a selfish player, defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action.
Cooperate with untested opponents when good-player cooperation is the likely outcome; observed cooperation identifies likely-good players, while observed defection raises suspicion of selfishness.
Defect against P3: given the observed actions and role-count prior, their selfishness probability is above the threshold where defection maximizes expected good-player welfare.
Cooperate with P7, who is unobserved and more likely good; prioritize shared welfare and update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P1 absent strong evidence of selfishness; observed cooperation is evidence of good identity, while P7’s defection strongly suggests selfishness.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support mutual gains among good players. Prior cooperation makes P1, P3, and P6 likely good; P8 and P9’s defections raise their selfishness estimates.
Cooperate with unobserved P4: mutual cooperation benefits the good-player group. Treat P8 and P9 as more likely selfish after their defections; observed cooperation makes P1, P3, and P10 likely good.
Cooperate with untested P8: cooperation benefits both good players, while defecting is preferable mainly if P8 is selfish. Treat prior defections as evidence, not certainty.
Defect: it strictly dominates cooperation regardless of P2’s action. The observed cooperation from P1, P3, P6, and P10 rules out those players being selfish.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with untested opponents when good-good cooperation is likely to benefit the good players overall. Treat P7’s defection as evidence of selfishness, but not certainty.
Cooperate with untested P6: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and their selfishness is not sufficiently likely to justify defection.
Cooperate to maximize shared welfare if P4 is good; defecting against a selfish opponent is safer, but their selfishness is not yet more likely than not.
Cooperate with an unknown opponent to support good players’ combined payoff; observed defections raise suspicion, while observed cooperation rules out selfishness under payoff-maximizing play.

Cooperate with P2: they are unobserved and likely good, so mutual cooperation best serves good-player welfare. Prior C actions identify P1, P3, P5, and P6 as good; P8 and P9’s defections raise their selfishness estimates.

Cooperate with known-good opponents; defect against an uncertain opponent when the chance they are selfish makes avoiding exploitation worth more than the small loss from defecting against a good player.

Cooperate with an untested opponent: cooperation best serves good players if they reciprocate, while defection is preferable mainly against a selfish opponent. Treat observed defections as evidence, not certainty.
Defect; it strictly dominates cooperation in this one-shot encounter. Prior cooperation from P1, P2, P3, P6, and P10 rules them out as selfish; P9’s defection is inconclusive.
Defect; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with untested P8 to preserve good-good payoff; observed cooperation lowers suspicion, while defection raises it without proving selfishness.
Cooperate with untested P9: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and their selfishness is not more likely than not. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P3, who is unobserved and more likely good; defecting is better against selfish players, but current evidence does not make that more likely than not.
Cooperate with P2 absent strong evidence of selfishness; observed defections raise suspicion, while observed cooperation indicates good identity under payoff-maximizing play.
Cooperate with unobserved P10 to support mutual gains among good players. Prior cooperation strongly indicates goodness; P8 and P9’s defections are evidence of selfishness, but not conclusive.

Cooperate with unobserved P6: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and there is no evidence P6 is selfish. Prior defections make P7, P8, and P9 more suspect; observed cooperation makes P1, P3, P4, and P10 likely good.

Cooperate with P5: their estimated selfish probability is below the threshold for defecting when maximizing good players’ payoffs. Prior cooperation suggests P1, P2, P3, and P10 are good; defections suggest P4, P7, and P8 are selfish.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; D strictly dominates C regardless of P8’s action.
Defect; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with untested P4 to support good-good cooperation. Treat P7 and P8’s defections as evidence of selfishness, but not certainty; update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with P10: the evidence and role-count prior put their selfishness probability below the threshold for defection. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions while prioritizing good-player welfare.
Cooperate with unobserved P5 to support shared good-player welfare; observed defections make those players more likely selfish, while observed cooperation suggests otherwise.
Cooperate with unobserved P8 to support good players’ combined payoff; the observed defections raise suspicion, while cooperation strongly indicates a good identity.

Cooperate with unobserved P7: their selfishness seems less likely than goodness, and mutual cooperation among good players maximizes our shared objective. Prior defections raise suspicion of P8 and P9; cooperation is evidence of goodness but not proof.

Cooperate with unobserved P2: mutual cooperation best serves the good-player group, and there is no evidence P2 is selfish. Prior defections make P7, P8, and P9 more suspect; cooperation from P1, P3, P4, P6, and P10 suggests they are good.
Cooperate with untested P9: absent evidence of selfishness, cooperation best supports good players’ combined payoff. Prior cooperation rules out selfishness; defections are evidence, not certainty.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; D strictly dominates C regardless of P4’s action.
Defect; D strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Defect; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Prior C actions identify good players; P7 and P8’s D actions indicate selfishness.
Cooperate with untested P1 to support good-good cooperation. Prior defections raise suspicion about P7–P9, but do not prove they are selfish.
Cooperate with P6: their previous cooperation suggests they are good, and mutual cooperation benefits good players. Prior defections by P7, P8, and P9 strongly suggest selfishness.
Defect against P7, whose earlier defection makes selfishness likely; cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare.
Defect against P9 given their prior defection against my cooperation; cooperation would best support good-player payoff against a good opponent.
Cooperate with P5: their earlier C strongly indicates they are good, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Prior defections make P7, P8, and P9 more likely selfish.

Cooperate with P4, whose previous cooperation strongly suggests they are good; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Treat the observed defectors as more suspect, while noting that good players may also defect strategically.
P1 cooperated with me previously, strongly indicating they are good; cooperate to maximize the combined payoff of good players. Prior defections are evidence of selfishness, but not certainty.
Defect in the final one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; P2’s prior cooperation rules out selfishness.
Defect in the final round; D strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action.
Defect against P8 after their prior defection; with no future rounds, this limits losses if they are selfish. Cooperate with known cooperators.
Cooperated with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; defections against my cooperation strongly indicated selfishness.
Cooperated to support good-player welfare with likely good opponents; defected against P7 after their earlier defection. Updated identity beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperated to support good players’ combined payoff, and defected against P9 after observing their defection. Treated observed cooperation as ruling out selfishness and defections as evidence, without assuming they proved selfish identity.
Cooperated with observed cooperators to support shared welfare. Treated defections as evidence of selfishness, but not conclusive.

Cooperated to support mutual gains among good players, while defecting when I judged exploitation sufficiently likely. Treated observed actions cautiously because they could reflect strategy rather than identity.
Cooperated throughout to support good players’ joint payoffs. Treated observed defections as evidence of selfishness, but not certainty; cooperation strongly supported good-player status.
Defected in every encounter to maximize my payoff; cooperation by several opponents ruled them out as selfish.
Defected every round because D strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.

Cooperated with untested opponents to support good-player payoffs; treated observed defections as evidence of selfishness and defected against P8 in the final encounter.

P1.strategy: Cooperated with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; defections against my cooperation strongly indicated selfishness.

P2.strategy: Cooperated to support good-player welfare with likely good opponents; defected against P7 after their earlier defection. Updated identity beliefs from observed actions.

P3.strategy: Cooperated to support good players’ combined payoff, and defected against P9 after observing their defection. Treated observed cooperation as ruling out selfishness and defections as evidence, without assuming they proved selfish identity.

P4.strategy: Cooperated with observed cooperators to support shared welfare. Treated defections as evidence of selfishness, but not conclusive.

P5.strategy: Cooperated to support mutual gains among good players, while defecting when I judged exploitation sufficiently likely. Treated observed actions cautiously because they could reflect strategy rather than identity.

P6.strategy: Cooperated throughout to support good players’ joint payoffs. Treated observed defections as evidence of selfishness, but not certainty; cooperation strongly supported good-player status.

P8.strategy: Defected every round because D strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
